answer: Each identity delivers a juniper consignment to the wharf, where a prism splits verification into three spectrum bands. Each band needs a different wharf auditor's confirmation at 15, so one identity pays 45 in fees plus a 60-credit bond. A failed band docks 20 from the bond. The kth fake still pays 45 plus 60 at risk, unshared, so 1,000 fakes pay 45,000 in fees with 60,000 locked. An honest identity pays one 45 and recovers its 60 after three bands pass. A slice-rental ring fails because a rented band confirmation carries the wrong key, so the prism band is rejected and the bond is docked.
